audit_findings.title: The bridge may add cash already consumed by the Valco acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $447 million purchase price versus $507.575 million cash bridge; removing $447 million would reduce value by $2.60 per share, or 4.8% of base equity value, before recognizing Valco
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds pre-closing cash while OE excludes Valco's earnings and liabilities.
audit_findings.evidence: While we believe our current cash position is strong and will enable us to fund many of our foreseeable growth initiatives, including acquisitions and capital investments, rising interest rates or reduced access to debt financing could impact our ability to pursue these initiatives.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate whether Valco had closed by September 5, 2026, so an error is not yet established. If it had closed, however, up to 88.1% of the cash bridge could already have been deployed, creating a materially inconsistent perimeter. Valco's acquired operating value could offset some or all of the cash reduction, but that value is absent and unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing or termination announcement effective by September 5, 2026, then rerun with post-closing cash, debt and assumed liabilities plus consistently measured Valco OE.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $135.262 million of acquisition spending in 2025, $241.767 million in 2024 and $377.029 million over two years; acquisitions supplied 5 percentage points of 2025's 6% consolidated sales growth
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth increases forecast OE, while recurring purchase consideration is excluded from OE as an investing outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, net sales increased in all regions compared to 2024, driven mostly by acquisitions in the Contractor and Industrial segments.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that substantially all 2025 consolidated sales growth came from acquisitions, while the DCF assumes 6% to 8% growth without an acquisition-spending charge. It remains unresolved whether future growth can be organic, but historical acquisition outlays equal a large fraction of the $528.2 million anchor and are reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct organic and acquired growth for each historical year and rerun either with organically supportable growth or a recurring maintenance-acquisition deduction supported by the acquisition record.

audit_findings.title: The option ceiling is inconsistent with the equity numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $645.8 million of implied exercise proceeds from 9.777 million options at the June 2026 weighted-average $66.06 exercise price; $3.76 per valuation share if credited under the full-share ceiling
audit_findings.mechanism: All option shares are included in the denominator, but the corresponding exercise cash is omitted from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: There were approximately 9.8 million vested share options and share options expected to vest as of December 26, 2025 with an aggregate intrinsic value of $ 223 million, a weighted average exercise price of $ 61.38 and a weighted average contractual term of 5.2 years.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated numerator-denominator inconsistency, not merely a possibility. Crediting the implied proceeds would raise base value from $53.94 to approximately $57.70 per share and bull value from $59.85 to approximately $63.61. Although neither reaches the $77.88 market price, the roughly 7% base-value effect is material to the valuation output and margin-of-safety threshold.
audit_findings.action: Rerun using option-by-option treasury-stock or option-value dilution at the valuation date, reconciling the June 2026 options, subsequent exercises, cancellations and grants.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may benefit from an unusually low capital-spending year
audit_findings.magnitude: $54.331 million difference between the filed $100 million 2026 plan and $45.669 million 2025 additions, equal to 10.3% of anchor OE; mechanically recurring that difference would reduce base value by about $5.24 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated sustainable capital-expenditure deduction inflates anchor OE and every forecast and terminal cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Internally generated funds and unused financing sources are expected to provide the Company with the flexibility to meet its liquidity needs in 2026, including its capital expenditure plan of approximately $100 million, planned dividends estimated at $195 million, share repurchases and acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The low 2025 outlay and substantially higher 2026 plan demonstrate a potentially important normalization issue, but they do not prove that $100 million is maintenance capital because the plan may include growth projects. The disclosed gap is nevertheless large enough relative to anchor OE to be materially capable of changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the exact 2025 OE capital deduction and classify 2023-2026 expenditures between maintenance, capacity expansion and acquisition integration; rerun with a supported normalized maintenance-capital allowance.

audit_findings.title: Upfront license fees may be capitalized as recurring earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: A non-recurring license-fee contribution embedded in anchor OE is grown and capitalized through the terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The operating margin rate for this segment for the year increased 6 percentage points compared to last year mostly due to the favorable margin impact of upfront license fees in the electric motor product application.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that upfront license fees were a major cause of the Expansion Markets margin increase, but it does not disclose the fee amount, associated future performance costs or recurrence. The six-point margin increase on $167.912 million of segment sales corresponds to about $10.1 million, only 1.9% of anchor OE, but that is not a reliable fee measurement or ceiling because other segment changes may offset it. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2025 license-fee revenue and margin contribution, contract performance obligations and recurrence history, then remove the non-recurring after-tax OE contribution and rerun.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retirement claims may be missing from both owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $32.887 million combined 2025 pension and postretirement unfunded status, $5 million expected 2026 contributions, and $85.610 million latest retirement-benefits and deferred-compensation liability
audit_findings.mechanism: Any funding deficit not captured in projected OE would be deducted from the equity bridge or reflected through future cash contributions.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to contribute $ 3 million to its unfunded pension plans and $ 2 million to the postretirement medical plan in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The possible omission should be reconciled, but its scale cannot change the valuation conclusion. The filed unfunded pension and medical amounts total only $0.19 per valuation share and 0.36% of base equity value. Even conservatively deducting the entire latest $85.610 million balance-sheet category would reduce base value by only $0.50 per share, from $53.94 to about $53.44, still far below the $77.88 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile plan-level funded status, deferred compensation assets and liabilities, and cash contributions already reflected in OE; correct the bridge if needed, without reopening the valuation conclusion unless newer liabilities are materially larger.
